mission: Lock-in: Ben commits to pursuing Veraine and addressing the seal. The triple-layered lock-in mechanism activates — he can't walk away.
why_now: All information is on the table; the choice must be made
conflict: Ben's Lie drives his response: he takes ownership of the crisis because that's what Skywalkers do. The survivors depend on him. The seal is failing. Veraine is moving. Someone has to act, and Ben decides it's him — alone with his small group, without calling the Order.
turning_point: Torin asks a quiet question about the modern Jedi's relationship with the light/dark boundary. 'Gavran thought so too. Before.' — seeds his eventual turn. Ben files it away but doesn't process it.
opening_hook: Ben spreads the fortress data across the command table — Corridor maps, seal readings, Veraine's file — while Sera and Torin sort archive materials with the practiced efficiency of people who've done it together before
closing_hook: Ben sends a partial report to Luke — enough to explain the delay, not enough to reveal the scope. The institutional lie grows. The Steady Returns lifts off the plateau, pointed along the Corridor toward the first anchor node. The wrongness has a name now. It has coordinates. And someone else is following them.
emotional_trajectory: Overwhelmed assessment -> grim determination -> the quiet cost of choosing to carry this alone

stakes.personal: Ben's self-imposed burden — his Lie fully operational
stakes.interpersonal: The fragile group dynamic — Sera's conditional respect, Torin's warmth, Kael's distance, Desh's pragmatism
stakes.external: The clock is ticking on three fronts: seal degradation, Veraine's progress, and the Order's ignorance

setting: Fortress upper level -> departure from the uncharted world
sensory_details: The fortress shrinking below as they lift off; the wrongness receding behind but not disappearing — it's everywhere now, just concentrated there; five people in a ship built for two; the survivors' unfamiliarity with modern cockpit interfaces — Sera's fingers hovering over controls she doesn't recognize, Torin's careful observation, Kael's deliberate stillness
canon_elements_needed: Ben Skywalker communication protocols with Luke and the Jedi Order
Jedi Order institutional hierarchy for crisis reporting
Ruusan Corridor strategic geography and anchor node network
Post-Fate of the Jedi era Jedi Order operational capacity
Force technique lineage and transmission across eras
action_beats: Ben lays out fortress data and Corridor maps across the command table
Sera and Torin organize archive materials into tactical priority order from muscle memory
Ben composes a partial report to Luke on his datapad and transmits it before he can change his mind
The Steady Returns lifts off the mountain plateau, engines straining with five passengers aboard a ship built for two
notes: R05 partial — technique lineage first mentioned. H06 planted: Torin's quiet question seeds his turn fifteen chapters later. This is the most important hook plant in the chapter — understated, easy to miss on first read. Ben's lie_reinforced: the lock-in convinces him the burden is his because only he brought the survivors together.
